name: Useful capabilities
summary: Complete the task people actually need.
explanation: Build around a real task. Make the useful path complete, and check that people can reach the outcome they need.

name: Clear ownership
summary: One authority for each consequential fact.
icon: <circle cx="16" cy="7" r="4"/><path d="M16 11v6M6 22v-5h20v5"/><rect x="3" y="22" width="6" height="7" rx="1"/><rect x="23" y="22" width="6" height="7" rx="1"/>
explanation: Give each important fact one owner. Read and change it through that owner so different parts of the system cannot quietly disagree.

name: Understandable design
summary: Structure with clear responsibilities and reasons.
explanation: Make responsibilities and dependencies easy to follow. Keep the structure close to the problem, and explain decisions that the code cannot make obvious.

name: Coherent evolution
summary: Improve the whole. Retire what is replaced.
explanation: Change the connected parts together. Remove replaced behavior and obsolete paths so each improvement leaves a coherent system.

name: Faithful results
explanation: Preserve what inputs and outputs mean. Keep identity, units, ordering, and relationships intact when transforming or moving data.

name: Informed control
summary: Visible choices. Explicit permission and limits.
icon: <path d="M7 4v24M16 4v24M25 4v24"/><rect x="4" y="9" width="6" height="6" rx="1" fill="currentColor"/><rect x="13" y="20" width="6" height="6" rx="1" fill="currentColor"/><rect x="22" y="7" width="6" height="6" rx="1" fill="currentColor"/>
explanation: Make choices and consequences visible. Ask permission where it matters, respect limits, and let people stop or change course.

name: Honest state and effects
summary: Keep known outcomes and uncertainty distinct.
icon: <circle cx="16" cy="16" r="12"/><path d="M16 8v8l5 3M7 5l-3 3"/><circle cx="16" cy="16" r="1" fill="currentColor"/>
explanation: Report what is known to have happened. Keep pending, completed, failed, and uncertain outcomes distinct, especially after interruptions.

name: Usable interfaces
summary: Help people discover, understand, and act.
explanation: Help people find the next action and understand its result. Use clear labels, consistent controls, and feedback where the action happens.

name: Actionable failures
summary: Explain what failed and the next useful step.
explanation: Say what failed, why, and what can help next. Preserve useful diagnostic evidence without exposing sensitive information.

name: Dependable recovery
summary: Resume useful work while preserving obligations.
explanation: Design for interruption and retry. Resume useful work without losing commitments or repeating effects that may already have happened.

name: Bounded resource use
summary: Respect limits, including retries and failed work.
explanation: Bound time, memory, storage, and repeated work. Include failed attempts and retries in those limits, and stop when further work cannot help.

name: Trustworthy evidence
summary: Match every claim to relevant observations.
explanation: Check claims against observations that could reveal a mistake. Test the behavior people depend on, and state what the evidence does not establish.

name: Transferable knowledge
summary: Leave others able to continue responsibly.
explanation: Leave the reasoning and instructions needed to continue. Keep documentation close to the work and update it when behavior changes.

name: Protected information
summary: Protect sensitive information while preserving useful diagnosis.
explanation: Collect and expose only the information needed. Protect credentials and private data in storage, interfaces, logs, and diagnostics.

name: Reproducible results
summary: Preserve exact inputs, methods, and execution conditions.
explanation: Record the inputs, versions, configuration, and methods needed to repeat a result. Distinguish an exact reproduction from an approximation.

name: Reasoned improvement
summary: Diagnose the problem, justify the change, and test its effect.
explanation: Diagnose before changing. Explain why a change should help, then compare its observed effect with that expectation.

name: Verified completion
summary: Close consequential findings through correction and verification.
explanation: Finish the promised outcome and verify it where it matters. Resolve relevant findings, and report any remaining limits honestly.
